card.name: Until now, and past-tense setups
card.fires_on: The word "until" (usually "until now" or "until recently") in news-style prose, and sometimes other words that open a past-time or hypothetical clause, such as "that", "if", "had" and "never".

modes.label: Until now / until recently
modes.description: "Until" starts a sentence or clause that contrasts the past with the present.
modes.example: But<< until>> now, there was little genetic proof for

modes.label: Past or hypothetical clause openers
modes.description: Words like "if", "had" or "that" that lead into a past-perfect or counterfactual statement.
modes.example: Perhaps Newton himself could have put it to work<< if>> he had had suitable computing machinery.

card.writes: It pushes toward present-tense verbs like begins, becomes and gets, and away from past-tense verbs like was and did.
card.plain: It fires on words like "until" that mark a change from the past to now, and it pushes the text toward a present-tense verb.
